headline: Postseason bound as Sox prepare for a massive Guardians showdown
morning_brew: We are finally here, and I can finally let out the breath I have been holding since April because the Sox have officially punched their ticket to the postseason. It was a damn roller coaster, and there were plenty of nights I spent pacing my living room like a caged animal, but this group found a way to grind out enough wins to keep the dream alive. Clinching doesn't mean we just coast into October, though. We have six games left to sharpen the edges before the real madness begins, and proving we can hold our own against a team like Cleveland starting tomorrow is the perfect dress rehearsal.

The Guardians come into Fenway sitting pretty at the top of the AL Central, and this three-game set is exactly the kind of test we need to see where this rotation and bullpen really stack up. I am not saying I expect perfection, but seeing the guys play with focus and discipline would go a long way in calming my frayed nerves. My neighbor Rick has been in my ear all week with some half-baked theory that the league is rigging this series for the narrative, but I told him I am way too busy worrying about our own pitching staff to care about his latest umpire dossiers.

We have a busy stretch ahead at the Fens with the Cubs rolling in right after Cleveland wraps up, and then the Pats head down to Jacksonville for a Sunday showdown. Football season is finally starting to get its legs under it, and watching Drake Maye work this offense feels like the start of something legitimate. It is a great time to be a fan in the Hub, even if my blood pressure suggests I should probably have retired years ago.
